title: Vote early in person or by mail (absentee voting)
question: How can I vote early in person or by mail in Staunton, and what are the deadlines?
office: Voter Registration Office (General Registrar and Electoral Board)
summary: Any registered Staunton voter may vote absentee without giving a reason, early in person or by mail. Early voting needs no application and takes place at the Voter Registration Office in City Hall, 116 W. Beverley St.; for November 3, 2026 the state lists September 18 to 5:00 p.m. Saturday, October 31, plus weekend days. Bring ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement. To vote by mail, apply online or on the state form (the office mails one on request) so it arrives by 5:00 p.m. Friday, October 23, 2026. Return the ballot so it arrives by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it postmarked by Election Day to arrive by noon Friday, November 6. Envelope errors that would void a ballot received by Friday, October 30 can be cured until noon November 6.

legal_basis.quote: Any registered voter may vote by absentee ballot in accordance with the provisions of this chapter in any election in which he is qualified to vote.
Each electoral board shall appoint the general registrar for its city or county
The electoral board of each county and city shall provide for absentee voting in person in the office of the general registrar or a voter satellite office established pursuant to § 24.2-701.2 .
Absentee voting in person shall be available on the forty-fifth day prior to any election and shall continue until 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday immediately preceding the election.
An application shall not be required for any registered voter appearing in person to cast an absentee ballot pursuant to § 24.2-701.1 .
Any registered voter offering to vote absentee in person shall provide his name and his residence address in the county or city in which he is offering to vote.
Except as provided in subsection F, a registered voter voting by absentee ballot in person shall provide one of the forms of identification specified in subsection B of § 24.2-643 .

If he does not show one of the forms of identification specified in subsection B of § 24.2-643 , he shall be allowed to vote after signing a statement, subject to felony penalties for false statements pursuant to § 24.2-1016 , that he is the named registered voter he claims to be.

For purposes of this chapter, such offices shall be open to the public (i) a minimum of eight hours between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the first and second Saturday and (ii) a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the second and third Sunday immediately preceding all elections.
The electoral board or general registrar may provide for absentee voting in person in such offices on additional Sundays.
Any applicant who is in line to cast his ballot when the office of the general registrar or voter satellite office closes shall be permitted to cast his absentee ballot that day.

Not later than 55 days prior to any election, the general registrar shall post notice of all voter satellite office locations in the locality and the dates and hours of operation of each location in the office of the general registrar and on the official website for the county or city.

An application for an absentee ballot may be accepted the later of (i) 12 months before an election or (ii) the day following any election held in the twelfth month prior to the election in which the applicant is applying to vote.

An application that is completed in person at the same time that the applicant registers to vote shall be held and processed no sooner than the fifth day after the date that the applicant registered to vote

Any other application may be made by mail, by electronic or telephonic transmission to a facsimile device if one is available to the office of the general registrar or to the office of the Department if a device is not available locally, or by other means.
The application shall be made to the appropriate registrar no later than 5:00 p.m. on the eleventh day prior to the election in which the applicant offers to vote.
The applicant's printed name and the last four digits of the applicant's social security number.
Any registered voter shall be eligible to file a special application to receive absentee ballots for all elections in which he is eligible to vote.

The application for an absentee ballot shall provide space for the applicant to indicate that he will require assistance to vote his absentee ballot by reason of blindness, disability, or inability to read or write.

the general registrar shall not reject the application of any individual because of an error or omission on any record or paper relating to the application, if such error or omission is not material in determining whether such individual is qualified to vote absentee.

The general registrar shall make printed ballots available for absentee voting not later than 45 days prior to any election or within three business days of the receipt of a properly completed absentee ballot application, whichever is later.
An envelope, properly addressed and postage prepaid, for the return of the ballot to the general registrar by mail or by the applicant in person, or to a drop-off location.

After the voter has marked his absentee ballot, he shall (a) enclose the ballot in the envelope provided for that purpose, (b) seal the envelope, (c) fill in and sign the statement printed on the back of the envelope, (d) enclose the ballot envelope and any required assistance form within the envelope directed to the general registrar, and (e) seal that envelope.

A mailed absentee ballot shall be returned (i) by mail to the office of the general registrar, (ii) by the voter in person to the general registrar, or (iii) to a drop-off location established pursuant to § 24.2-707.1 .
Failure to follow the procedures set forth in this section shall render the applicant's ballot void.

The general registrar of each county or city shall establish at the office of the general registrar and each voter satellite office in operation for an election a drop-off location for the purpose of allowing the deposit of completed absentee ballots for such election.
On the day of the election, there shall also be a drop-off location at each polling place in operation for the election.

Not later than 55 days prior to any election, the general registrar shall post notice of the sites of the drop-off locations in the locality in the office of the general registrar and on the official website of the county or city.
Absentee ballots shall be returned to the general registrar or to a drop-off location before the closing of the polls.
Any voter who is in line to return an absentee ballot at a drop-off location by 7:00 p.m. on the day of the election shall be permitted to deposit his absentee ballot.

any absentee ballot (i) returned to the general registrar after the closing of the polls on election day but before noon on the third day after the election and (ii) postmarked on or before the date of the election shall be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if the voter is found entitled to vote.

Within three days of such finding, the registrar shall notify the voter in writing or by email of the error or failure and shall provide information to the voter on how to correct the issue so his ballot may be counted.

The voter shall be entitled to make such necessary corrections before noon on the third day after the election, and his ballot shall then be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if he is found to be entitled to vote.
Any person who has applied for and received an absentee ballot may choose not to vote absentee and shall be entitled to cast a ballot in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

Any person who has applied for and has been sent an absentee ballot but does not receive the ballot or loses the ballot shall be entitled to cast a ballot in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

Any person registered and otherwise qualified to vote may request at any time prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day preceding the election that he be permitted to vote by emergency absentee ballot with the assistance of his designated representative.

A qualified voter may vote absentee in person in the office of the general registrar through 2:00 p.m. on the day immediately preceding the election by complying with the requirements of § 24.2-643 and affirming that one of the following emergency circumstances will prevent him from voting on election day:
The Secretary, in coordination with local election officials, shall implement a free-access system by which a voter may determine:

The electoral board of each county and city shall send a written explanation of the reason for rejection of an absentee ballot to the voter whose absentee ballot is rejected within 90 days of the date on which the ballot is rejected.

An officer of election, by a written notice given to the voter, shall inform him that a determination of his right to vote shall be made by the electoral board and advise the voter of the beginning time and place for the board's meeting and of the voter's right to be present at that meeting.
A central absentee voter precinct shall be made by the governing body by ordinance; the ordinance shall state for which elections the precinct shall be used.
The circuit courts shall have jurisdiction to issue an injunction to enforce the provisions of this section upon the application of (i) any aggrieved voter
The electoral board may institute proceedings pursuant to § 24.2-234.1 for the removal of any general registrar by a recorded majority vote of the Board after a public hearing on related matters.

The State Board, through the Department of Elections, shall supervise and coordinate the work of the county and city electoral boards and of the registrars to obtain uniformity in their practices and proceedings and legality and purity in all elections.

Any willfully false material statement or entry made by any person in any statement, form, or report required by this title shall constitute the crime of election fraud and be punishable as a Class 5 felony.
The registration records shall be closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election.
any person who is qualified to register to vote shall be entitled to register in person up to and including the day of the election
Except as provided in § 24.2-703 or 24.2-703.1 , a separate application shall be completed for each election in which the applicant offers to vote.
However, an applicant completing the application in person shall not be required to provide the last four digits of his social security number
The expiration date on a Virginia driver's license shall not be considered when determining the validity of the driver's license offered for purposes of this section.
The general registrar shall note on each application received whether the applicant is or is not a registered voter.

A voter's failure to provide the date, or any part of the date, including the year, on which he signed the statement printed on the back of the envelope shall not be considered a material omission and shall not render his ballot void.
For any absentee ballot received by the Friday immediately preceding the day of the election
and such error or failure would render the ballot void by law
The general registrar may issue a new absentee ballot to the voter if necessary and shall preserve the first ballot with other spoiled ballots.
The voter may, prior to the day of the election, return the ballot to the general registrar (i) unopened in the sealed envelope in which it was sent to him or (ii) opened and unmarked.

On the day of the election, (a) if the general registrar or an officer of election is able to confirm the return of the unused ballot, the voter shall be entitled to vote a regular ballot and (b) if the general registrar or an officer of election is unable to confirm the return of the unused ballot, the voter shall be entitled to cast a provisional ballot pursuant to § 24.2-653.1 .
The voter may, on the day of the election, return his unused ballot to his proper polling place or central absentee voter precinct, and the unused ballot shall be preserved with other unused ballots.

The voter may, on the day of the election, offer to vote at his proper polling place or at a central absentee voter precinct, and he shall be entitled to cast a provisional ballot pursuant to § 24.2-653.1 .

The voter may, prior to the day of the election, present the defaced ballot to the general registrar or an officer of election, and the ballot shall be marked spoiled by the general registrar or an officer of election and placed in a spoiled-ballot envelope to be retained with the ballots for the election.

A person with a disability or illness who has applied for and has been sent an absentee ballot who did not receive or has lost the absentee ballot on or before the Saturday before the election may obtain a replacement absentee ballot.
In such case, the voter may request a replacement absentee ballot by the close of business for the local elections office on the Saturday before election day

The representative designated by a voter for purposes of this subsection shall be age 18 or older and shall not be an elected official, a candidate for elected office, or the deputy, spouse, parent, or child of an elected official or candidate.

His signature shall be witnessed by the designated representative, who shall sign and return the completed form to the office of the general registrar no later than 5:00 p.m. on the day preceding the election.
The ballot shall be counted only if the ballot is received by the general registrar prior to the close of polls

After 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election, an obligation arose that requires the voter be absent from his county or city on election day for (i) his business, profession, or occupation; (ii) the hospitalization of the voter or a member of his immediate family; or (iii) the death of a member of his immediate family.

At all elections, the polls shall be open at each polling place at 6:00 a.m. on the day of the election and closed at 7:00 p.m. on the same day except as provided for central absentee voter precincts pursuant to subsection G of § 24.2-712 .
If the voter is voting provisionally as required by § 24.2-643
where such neglect, misuse, or incompetence has a material adverse effect upon the conduct of the office

Any general registrar may be removed from office by the circuit court in whose jurisdiction he serves upon a petition signed by a majority of the members of the State Board as provided in § 24.2-103 or a majority of the members of his local electoral board as provided in § 24.2-109 .
The following omissions are always material and any Envelope B containing such omissions shall be rendered invalid if any of the following exists:
The voter did not provide the voter's birth year; or
The voter omitted the date, or provided an incorrect or incomplete date on which the voter signed Envelope B;
The voter did not provide either the voter's city or zip code;
The voter used the voter's first initial instead of the voter's first full name, so long as the voter provided the voter's full middle name;

If there is no evidence from the Intelligent Mail barcode that the ballot was mailed after the close of polls for the relevant election and if the return envelope has a missing postmark, the ballot shall be rendered invalid.

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 1.10.010 (Absentee voter election district; on eCode360, paraphrased in caveats, not quoted)

steps.step: Make sure you are registered to vote at your Staunton address
steps.how: Check or update your registration on the Virginia Citizen Portal, or call the Voter Registration Office. You can vote early, and get a mail ballot, only from the locality where you are registered. If you register in person and apply for a mail ballot at the same time, the application is processed no sooner than the fifth day after you registered. State law closes the registration records during the 10 days before the election. After the registration deadline you can still register and vote in person with a provisional ballot (same-day registration; see the voter registration process).
steps.deadline: For the November 3, 2026 election the Department of Elections lists October 23, 2026 as the last day to register or update a registration
steps.quote: Voters are only allowed to vote early in the locality in which they are registered.

steps.step: Choose how to vote absentee: early in person, or by mail
steps.how: No reason is needed for either. Voting early in person needs no application. Voting by mail needs an application for each election, unless you join the permanent absentee list, which sends you a ballot for every election you are eligible to vote in.
steps.quote: No excuse is needed to vote early.

steps.step: Early in person: go to the Voter Registration Office in City Hall during the early voting period
steps.how: Early voting is in Staunton City Hall, 116 W. Beverley St. (the city calls it the City Hall Lobby; the office is on the 1st floor, down the hall from the front doors at the counter before Council Chambers, on the left). No other early voting site is listed on the city pages read. The city's How to Vote page gives early voting hours of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., closed on holidays and during inclement weather in line with City closures. For the November 3, 2026 election the Department of Elections lists early voting from Friday, September 18 through 5:00 p.m. Saturday, October 31, and says registrar offices will be open on Sunday, October 18, Saturday, October 24, Sunday, October 25 and Saturday, October 31. State law requires at least eight hours between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on those two Saturdays and at least five hours between 11:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on those two Sundays, and the city says the office is open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on the Saturday before every general election. Staunton's own hours for the other weekend days were not read (for the August 4, 2026 primary the city listed Saturdays 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Sundays 12:00 to 5:00 p.m.); the Department says to contact the registrar for early voting and satellite location details. Anyone in line when the office closes may still vote that day.
steps.deadline: Early voting ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election (October 31, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)
steps.quote: Vote early at Staunton City Hall Lobby starting 45 days before Election Day.

steps.step: Early in person: give your name and address, show ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement, and vote
steps.who: Voter; the registrar's staff and officers of election at the office
steps.how: Give your name and residence address and show an acceptable ID. The state's list includes a Virginia driver's license or DMV ID card (current or expired), a U.S. passport, a photo employee ID, a student ID from a Virginia school or college, a Department of Elections voter ID card, and a current utility bill, bank statement, government check or paycheck with your name and address; an out-of-state driver's license is not accepted. Without ID, sign an ID Confirmation Statement and vote a regular ballot. A voter who does neither is offered a provisional ballot and has until noon on the Friday after the election to give the electoral board a copy of ID or a signed statement. The Department of Elections says accessible equipment and curbside voting are available on request. Curbside voting is offered to voters 65 or older or with a physical disability: park in a designated spot (left side of Central Avenue across from the "You Belong Here" mural, or two spots in the old SunTrust lot near the "Antiques" building and the police department) and follow the signs; a helper may go inside, or call ahead.
steps.quote: Bring an acceptable form of ID and provide your name and address.

steps.step: By mail: apply for a mail ballot
steps.how: Staunton lists three ways: apply online through the Virginia Citizen Portal (the Department's step-by-step guide, written for joining the permanent list online, asks for a Virginia driver's license or state ID number, date of birth and Social Security number); call the office at (540) 332-3840 to have a paper application sent; or print the Virginia Absentee Ballot Application (SBE-701/703.1) and mail it to P.O. Box 1092, Staunton, VA 24402. The state form and the Department's page also accept a signed application by fax or as a scanned email attachment, and an application can be completed at the office. Give your name and the last four digits of your Social Security number (the form says the application is denied without them; the digits are not required when the application is completed in person at the office), your Staunton registration address, the election, a different mailing address if needed, and your signature. Answer Yes in Section 4 to join the permanent absentee list. Check Section 7c if you need help marking the ballot (an assistance form comes with it) or are print-disabled (a screen-reader ballot). An application may be accepted from 12 months before the election (or from the day after an election held in that twelfth month, if later).
steps.deadline: Received by 5:00 p.m. on the 11th day before the election (5:00 p.m., Friday, October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)
steps.quote: You can apply for an absentee ballot in one of three ways:

steps.step: By mail: the registrar reviews the application and mails the ballot
steps.how: The registrar notes on each application whether you are a registered voter. An error or omission that is not material to whether you are qualified cannot be a reason to reject the application. If the application is properly completed and signed and you are registered in Staunton, the registrar sends the ballot by first-class or expedited mail (or hands it to you at the office). State law requires ballots to be available no later than 45 days before the election, or within three business days of receiving a properly completed application, whichever is later; the Department says ballots can be mailed starting 45 days before the election. The mailing holds the ballot, the envelope with the Statement of Voter (Envelope B), a postage-prepaid return envelope, and instructions that list the drop-off locations, plus an assistance form if you asked for help.
steps.deadline: Ballots made available no later than 45 days before the election, or within three business days of receiving a properly completed application, whichever is later
steps.quote: The general registrar shall make printed ballots available for absentee voting not later than 45 days prior to any election or within three business days of the receipt of a properly completed absentee ballot application, whichever is later.

steps.step: By mail: track your application and ballot
steps.how: The Citizen Portal shows whether your application was received and accepted and your absentee ballot status. The Department's page points to Ballot Scout for tracking a mailed ballot. If the ballot does not arrive in time, call the office at (540) 332-3840 or email vote@ci.staunton.va.us.
steps.quote: If you have submitted an absentee ballot application for a ballot to be sent by mail, you can track your ballot by logging into Ballot Scout.

steps.step: By mail: mark the ballot and complete Envelope B
steps.who: Voter (and an assistant, if you asked for help)
steps.how: Mark the ballot privately and seal it in Envelope B. Fill in and sign the Statement of Voter on Envelope B: your full name, your residence address, the last four digits of your Social Security number and your birth year. Under 1VAC20-70-20(B) the ballot is invalid if Envelope B has no signature, no last name, no first name (a first initial is enough if you give your full middle name), no house number and street name or rural route, neither a city nor a ZIP code, no birth year, or no last four Social Security digits (or, for a voter never issued a number, the unique identifier), or leaves out a generational suffix needed to tell same-named voters at one address apart. The cure process (s10) can fix these only on ballots received by the Friday before the election. A missing middle name, a missing city or ZIP code when the other is given, or a missing or wrong date does not void the ballot. If you asked for assistance, complete and sign the assistance form sent with the ballot. Put Envelope B (and any assistance form) in the return envelope and seal it.
steps.quote: After the voter has marked his absentee ballot, he shall (a) enclose the ballot in the envelope provided for that purpose, (b) seal the envelope, (c) fill in and sign the statement printed on the back of the envelope, (d) enclose the ballot envelope and any required assistance form within the envelope directed to the general registrar, and (e) seal that envelope.

steps.how: Return it by mail in the postage-prepaid envelope (mail includes a commercial delivery service, but not a personal courier or another person), in person to the Voter Registration Office in City Hall, or at a drop-off location. State law requires a drop-off location at the registrar's office and, on Election Day, at each polling place; the sites are listed in the instructions mailed with the ballot. No Staunton page read gives a drop box location; the Department's page says to contact the registrar for ballot drop box information.
steps.deadline: Received at the Voter Registration Office or a drop-off location before the polls close at 7:00 p.m. on Election Day, however it is returned (anyone in line at a drop-off location at 7:00 p.m. may deposit the ballot); a mailed ballot that arrives later counts only if postmarked on or before Election Day and received by noon on the third day after (Friday, November 6, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election). Under 1VAC20-70-20(F), a late-arriving mailed ballot with a missing postmark is invalid, and one with an illegible postmark is checked against its mail barcode and the Envelope B date, so mail it early.
steps.fee: None: the return envelope is postage prepaid
steps.quote: Complete and return your ballot to your local general registrar's office by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.

steps.step: If the registrar finds a problem with your returned ballot, correct it (cure)
steps.who: General Registrar notifies; the voter corrects
steps.how: For a ballot received by the Friday before the election, if the Statement of Voter was not filled out correctly or completely, or a required step was missed, and the error would make the ballot void by law, the registrar records the issue and tells you in writing or by email how to fix it. The registrar may issue a new ballot. Contact the office promptly.
steps.deadline: The registrar notifies within three days of finding the problem; the voter corrects it before noon on the third day after the election (Friday, November 6, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)
steps.quote: Within three days of such finding, the registrar shall notify the voter in writing or by email of the error or failure and shall provide information to the voter on how to correct the issue so his ballot may be counted.

steps.step: If your mail ballot never arrives, is lost or damaged, or you change your mind, vote in person instead
steps.who: Voter; General Registrar or officers of election
steps.how: Ballot never arrived or was lost: before Election Day, give the registrar (or an officer of election) a signed statement that the ballot did not arrive or was lost, and you may then vote a regular ballot (at the office during early voting). On Election Day you may vote at your polling place, but only a provisional ballot. Unused or damaged ballot: before Election Day, return it to the registrar (unopened, or opened and unmarked; a damaged ballot is marked spoiled) and vote a regular ballot at the office, or vote at your polling place on Election Day (a regular ballot if the officers can confirm the return, otherwise a provisional ballot); or bring the unused or damaged ballot to your polling place on Election Day and vote a regular ballot. Going to the polls on Election Day without it means a provisional ballot. State law also lets these voters use a central absentee voter precinct on Election Day, but the city says there is no voting in City Hall on Election Day: go to the polling place for your ward (polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.). A voter with a disability or illness whose ballot did not arrive or was lost by the Saturday before the election may instead request a replacement ballot by close of business that Saturday and name in writing a representative (18 or older, not an elected official, a candidate, or the deputy, spouse, parent or child of one) who collects it and returns it as the registrar directs by the close of polls, on the State Board's form (not located on the pages read; ask the office).
steps.deadline: Early voting at the office ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election; a replacement ballot (Va. Code § 24.2-703.2) must be requested by close of business that Saturday and returned by the close of polls; polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day
steps.quote: Any person who has applied for and has been sent an absentee ballot but does not receive the ballot or loses the ballot shall be entitled to cast a ballot in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

steps.step: In an emergency after the deadline, ask for an emergency absentee ballot
steps.who: Voter; a designated representative; General Registrar
steps.how: Use the Emergency Absentee Ballot Application (ELECT-705, Section 1b) if (i) you could not apply by the deadline because of your hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness or death of your spouse, child or parent, or another emergency; (ii) such an emergency arising after the application deadline will keep you from voting on Election Day; or (iii) you applied in time, your ballot had not arrived within 10 days of the election, and such an emergency will keep you from voting on Election Day. You sign the form in front of your designated representative (18 or older, and not an elected official, a candidate, or the deputy, spouse, parent or child of one), who signs it and returns it to the office. The registrar gives the ballot to the representative, who delivers it, watches you mark and seal it, and returns it to the office. Separately (Section 1a of the same form), if after 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election an obligation arose that requires you to be away from Staunton on Election Day for your business, profession or occupation, your own or an immediate family member's hospitalization, or a death in your immediate family (or you are an officer of election assigned after that time to a precinct other than your own), you may vote in person at the office through 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election, showing ID or signing the ID Confirmation Statement.
steps.deadline: Request before 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election; the completed form returned by 5:00 p.m. that day; the ballot counts only if the registrar receives it before the polls close. The in-person route (Section 1a) ends at 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election
steps.quote: Any person registered and otherwise qualified to vote may request at any time prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day preceding the election that he be permitted to vote by emergency absentee ballot with the assistance of his designated representative.

steps.step: After the election: if your absentee ballot was rejected, you receive a written reason
steps.how: If an absentee ballot is not counted, the electoral board must send the voter a written explanation of the reason. You can also check the ballot's status on the Citizen Portal. No appeal of a rejected ballot was found in the sections read (see escalation for the cure and other routes).
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the date the ballot is rejected
steps.quote: The electoral board of each county and city shall send a written explanation of the reason for rejection of an absentee ballot to the voter whose absentee ballot is rejected within 90 days of the date on which the ballot is rejected.

escalation.trigger: Mail ballot application not accepted (for example, the last four digits of the Social Security number or the signature are missing)
escalation.next: General Registrar: send a corrected application before the deadline, or vote early in person instead (no application needed)
escalation.deadline: 5:00 p.m. on the 11th day before the election for a mail ballot (October 23, 2026); 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election for early voting in person (October 31, 2026)
escalation.quote: the general registrar shall not reject the application of any individual because of an error or omission on any record or paper relating to the application, if such error or omission is not material in determining whether such individual is qualified to vote absentee.

escalation.trigger: Returned mail ballot received by the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026) has a defect that would make it void (for example, no signature, birth year or last four Social Security digits on Envelope B)
escalation.next: General Registrar (cure: correct the Statement of Voter, or vote a new ballot the registrar issues)
escalation.deadline: Before noon on the third day after the election (November 6, 2026)
escalation.quote: The voter shall be entitled to make such necessary corrections before noon on the third day after the election, and his ballot shall then be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if he is found to be entitled to vote.

escalation.trigger: Mail ballot never arrived or was lost
escalation.next: General Registrar before Election Day (signed statement, then a regular ballot), or your ward's polling place on Election Day (provisional ballot, decided by the Staunton Electoral Board)
escalation.deadline: Statement before Election Day; or at the polls on Election Day, 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.
escalation.quote: The voter may, prior to the day of the election, present to the general registrar or officer of election a statement signed by him that he did not receive the ballot or has lost the ballot.

escalation.trigger: Requested ballot not received within 10 days of the election, and the voter's hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness or death of a spouse, child or parent, or another emergency will keep the voter from the polls
escalation.next: General Registrar: emergency absentee ballot delivered through a designated representative
escalation.deadline: Request before 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election; form returned by 5:00 p.m. that day
escalation.quote: has applied to receive an absentee ballot by the deadline but has not received his ballot within 10 days of the election and will be unable to vote on election day due to his hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness, or death of a spouse, child, or parent, or other emergency found to justify receipt of an emergency absentee ballot.

escalation.trigger: Voted a provisional ballot (for example, at early voting without showing ID or signing the ID Confirmation Statement)
escalation.next: Staunton Electoral Board, which decides whether the provisional ballot counts; any provisional voter may attend the board's meeting, and a voter who voted provisionally for lack of ID may send the board a copy of ID or a signed statement by fax, email, in person or mail
escalation.deadline: ID or signed statement received by the electoral board no later than noon on the third day after the election
escalation.quote: to be received by the electoral board no later than noon on the third day after the election.

escalation.trigger: Unhappy with how the Voter Registration Office handled an application, a ballot or a visit
escalation.next: Staunton Electoral Board (StauntonElectoralBoard@ci.staunton.va.us), which appoints the General Registrar (Va. Code § 24.2-109(A)) and may begin removal proceedings (a petition to the circuit court, § 24.2-234.1(B)) for neglect of a clear ministerial duty, misuse of the office or incompetence that has a material adverse effect on the conduct of the office; the city pages read describe no complaint procedure
escalation.quote: The electoral board may institute proceedings pursuant to § 24.2-234.1 for the removal of any general registrar by a recorded majority vote of the Board after a public hearing on related matters.

escalation.trigger: The registrar does not process an application or send a ballot as the law requires
escalation.next: Circuit court, presumably the Staunton Circuit Court (injunction to enforce Va. Code § 24.2-706, on the application of an aggrieved voter; the statute does not name the venue)
escalation.quote: The circuit courts shall have jurisdiction to issue an injunction to enforce the provisions of this section upon the application of (i) any aggrieved voter

escalation.trigger: The local office or electoral board does not follow election law
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections and the State Board of Elections, which supervise local electoral boards and registrars (the Department's contact page links a Virginia Voters' Election Day Complaint Form; under § 24.2-103(E) the State Board may also begin removal proceedings against a general registrar)
escalation.quote: The State Board, through the Department of Elections, shall supervise and coordinate the work of the county and city electoral boards and of the registrars to obtain uniformity in their practices and proceedings and legality and purity in all elections.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The registrar pages' newest copies are from May to July 2026 (How to Vote, Voter Registration, Where to Vote, Electoral Board and Upcoming Elections), and later copies of other city pages hold a bot-check page instead of content, so a newer copy is unlikely. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act. The How to Vote menu also lists a separate Vote By Mail page (www.ci.staunton.va.us/departments/voter-registration/how-to-vote/vote-by-mail) that has no archived copy; it may give drop box, fax or email details not recorded here.

November 2026 local details not confirmed: the copies predate the city's notice for the November 3, 2026 election, which state law requires 55 days before (by September 9, 2026) for any voter satellite office and for the drop-off sites (Va. Code §§ 24.2-701.2(E), 24.2-707.1(C)). The Upcoming Elections copy says only 'Stay tuned for more information' for November. The November dates recorded here (early voting September 18 to 5:00 p.m. October 31, weekend days October 18, 24, 25 and 31, application deadline 5:00 p.m. October 23, registration deadline October 23) come from the Virginia Department of Elections' Upcoming Elections page and the statutes, not from a Staunton notice.

Weekend and daily hours: the city's How to Vote copy gives early voting hours of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its Voter Registration copy says the office opens at 8:30 a.m. (regular hours 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.) and, for the August 2026 primary, that voting began at 9:00 a.m. The Voter Registration copy also says the office opens for in-person absentee voting on the Saturday before general elections from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Staunton's hours for Sunday, October 18, Saturday, October 24, Sunday, October 25 and Saturday, October 31, 2026 were not found; the August 2026 primary schedule (Saturdays 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Sundays 12:00 to 5:00 p.m., described as new) is the closest local precedent. Sunday hours appear to follow 2026 amendments to Va. Code § 24.2-701.1 (history line: 2026, cc. 945, 1078).

Start date: Va. Code § 24.2-701.1(A) makes early voting available on the 45th day before an election. For November 3, 2026 that is Saturday, September 19, but the Department of Elections gives Friday, September 18. Staunton followed the same pattern in 2025 (its November 4, 2025 schedule began Friday, September 19, the 46th day). The reason for the earlier start was not found in the index text.

Drop box: no Staunton page read names a ballot drop box or its location. Va. Code § 24.2-707.1(A) requires a drop-off location at the registrar's office and at each polling place on Election Day; the Department's page says the sites are listed in the instructions mailed with the ballot.

Application channels: the city's page lists online, a paper application requested by phone, and a printed application mailed to P.O. Box 1092. The state form and the Department's page also accept email and fax. No fax number for the Staunton office appears on the pages read, and the city page does not say whether vote@ci.staunton.va.us takes scanned applications; the office mailbox is recorded as published on the Voter Registration page.

Online application and tracking: the Citizen Portal (vote.elections.virginia.gov) refuses automated readers, and the state ballot status login linked from the city page and Ballot Scout ask for voter details, so none of them is described here. The identity details required online are taken from the Department's Absentee and Early Voting page.

Election Day: the city's Where to Vote copy says no voting takes place in City Hall on Election Day and voters must go to their assigned precinct. Staunton City Code § 1.10.010 (read on eCode360; paraphrased, not quoted) establishes one central absentee voter election district in City Hall to receive, count and record all absentee ballots cast in the city, citing Va. Code §§ 24.2-710 through 24.2-712; its history note traces it to a 1982 ordinance carried into the 1985 Code, and it still refers to general elections in May and November. Va. Code §§ 24.2-708 and 24.2-712(C) let a voter bring an unmarked ballot to a central absentee voter precinct on Election Day; whether Staunton's central absentee precinct accepts voters that way was not found, so this record follows the city's instruction to go to the precinct.

Local law: Staunton's City Code is published by General Code on eCode360, whose terms limit content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes, so no City Code text is quoted. eCode360 notes its copy may not reflect the latest legislation. The Title 1 and Title 2 tables of contents list no ordinance creating a voter satellite office (Va. Code § 24.2-701.2(A)); none was found.

Versions: the index marks Va. Code §§ 24.2-653, 24.2-706, 24.2-709, 24.2-709.1 and 24.2-711.1 'effective until January 1, 2027' and § 24.2-703.1 (permanent absentee list) 'effective until July 1, 2027', and holds no successor text. They govern the November 3, 2026 election; re-check deadlines, the cure process and the permanent list for later elections. The index text of §§ 24.2-701.1, 24.2-705, 24.2-706 and 24.2-707.1 already includes 2026 amendments (per their history lines).

Rejected applications: the state form's Privacy Act notice says an application will be denied without the last four digits of the Social Security number. No statute read requires the registrar to notify an applicant whose mail ballot application is rejected, and no appeal route for a rejected application or a rejected ballot was found. The routes recorded are a corrected application or in-person voting, the cure process, the electoral board's written explanation after the election (§ 24.2-711.1(B)), the electoral board's oversight of the registrar, the Department and State Board, and an injunction under § 24.2-706(G).
Cure coverage: the notice duty in § 24.2-709.1(C) covers ballots received by the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026); how the office handles defects on ballots received later was not found.

Fees: no source read states a fee for applying for or voting an absentee ballot. The cost of returning a ballot by a commercial delivery service is not stated; the postage-paid envelope covers U.S. mail.

ID list: the city's 'Acceptable Forms of ID' PDF has no archived copy and was not read; the ID examples come from the Department's Voter Identification chart (Rev. 09/2026), which cites Va. Code § 24.2-643(B).

Forms: the Department's page labels SBE-703.1C 'Permanent Absentee Application', but the PDF is the Permanent Absentee Voter Change Form for voters already on the list; joining the list is done in Section 4 of SBE-701/703.1 or online. SBE-703.1C has a PDF form dictionary with an empty field list, so it is recorded as not fillable. The city's 2024 How to Vote page linked a city-hosted copy of the application; the 2026 page links none, so only the Department's copies are recorded.

Emergency ballots: the ELECT-705 instructions say the voted ballot 'needs a postmark dated on or before election day', but Va. Code § 24.2-705(A) counts an emergency ballot only if the general registrar receives it before the polls close; this record follows the statute. The State Board form for a replacement ballot under § 24.2-703.2 was not located on the pages read.

Postmarks: under 1VAC20-70-20(F), a mailed ballot received by noon on the third day after the election with a missing or illegible postmark is checked against its Intelligent Mail barcode; it is invalid if the barcode shows it was mailed after the polls closed or if the postmark is missing, and an illegible postmark is judged by the date the Envelope B oath was signed.
Court: Va. Code § 24.2-706(G) gives the circuit courts jurisdiction without naming a venue; the Staunton Circuit Court is the presumed court for a Staunton voter, not a rule found in the text.

Ballot mailing date: Va. Code § 24.2-612 sets a deadline ('not later than 45 days prior' or three business days after a complete application, whichever is later); the Department's page and the state form describe ballots as available or mailed starting 45 days before the election.
Curbside voting: the city's page describes curbside spots at City Hall and says a helper may call ahead, but gives no separate curbside phone number; the office number is the published line.

Electoral Board: the board page lists members with individual mailboxes, which are not recorded; the board's general mailbox is recorded. The page copy lists a June 5, 2026 meeting; later meeting dates were not read.

Not modeled: military and overseas (UOCAVA) voters, who may apply on the Federal Post Card Application and get ballots by email or fax, with a later return deadline (§§ 24.2-702.1, 24.2-703, 24.2-709(C)); first-time federal voters who registered by mail and must include a copy of ID with the ballot; and the details of the screen-reader ballot for print-disabled voters (§ 24.2-704(B)).
Names: the city pages name the Director of Elections and General Registrar and the Electoral Board members, and the court page names the clerk and judges; no names are recorded here.

corrections: Quotes: all 71 original quotes were confirmed. The 61 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), and each subsection label matches the text. The 7 web quotes match exactly: 4 against the Internet Archive copy of the city's How to Vote page (May 11, 2026), 3 against the Department of Elections' Absentee and Early Voting and Early Voting Office Locations pages, read live on 2026-10-11 with the research User-Agent. The 3 quotes from 1VAC20-70-20 match law.lis.virginia.gov, read the same day. 28 quotes were added and checked the same way: 25 state-law quotes (Va. Code §§ 24.2-416(A), 24.2-420.1(A), 24.2-603, 24.2-643(B), 24.2-653(B), 24.2-701(A) and (C)(1), 24.2-703.2 (two), 24.2-705(A) (three) and (B)(1), 24.2-706(B), 24.2-707(A), 24.2-708(A)(1) (two), (A)(2), (B)(2) and (C)(1), 24.2-709.1(C) (three), 24.2-109(B), 24.2-234.1(B)) and 3 from 1VAC20-70-20 ((B)(5), (C)(2), (F)(3)). After the edits, lexflow's own checker (municipal.places.check_quotes) matched 86 of 86 code quotes.

Summary: 'Envelope errors can be cured by then' overstated the cure. The § 24.2-709.1(C) notice-and-cure process covers only ballots received by the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026), and only errors that would void the ballot. The summary now says so.

s6: 'Ballots go out from 45 days before the election' misstated § 24.2-612, which sets a deadline ('not later than 45 days prior', or three business days after a complete application, whichever is later). The step and its deadline now say 'no later than', and the Department's 'starting 45 days prior' is given as the Department's statement. Added the § 24.2-706(B) note of registration and the § 24.2-706(C) first-class or expedited mailing.

s7: removed the claim that the city's How to Vote page links the state's ballot status sign-in. The archived page links only the Citizen Portal, and the Voter Registration page links the online application; the Department's Citizen Portal page is what describes absentee ballot status.

s8: the list of material omissions now follows 1VAC20-70-20(B). It adds the generational suffix case, the first-initial exception ((C)(2)) and the both-city-and-ZIP rule ((B)(5)), and it says house number and street name or rural route rather than 'street address'. 'Unless it is cured' now says the cure covers only ballots received by the Friday before the election.

s9: the deadline read as if a mailed ballot always needs an Election Day postmark. Any ballot received by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day counts (§ 24.2-709(A)); the postmark rule applies only to mailed ballots that arrive later (§ 24.2-709(B)). Added the missing and illegible postmark rule of 1VAC20-70-20(F), and the Department's note to contact the registrar for drop box information.
s10: added the § 24.2-709.1(C) condition that the error or failure 'would render the ballot void by law'.

s11: the draft mixed up the § 24.2-708 cases. 'Unless the officers can confirm the return' applies only to an unused or damaged ballot handed back to the registrar before Election Day ((A)(1), (C)(1)). A voter whose ballot never arrived or was lost can vote only a provisional ballot on Election Day ((B)(2)). The step now treats the two cases separately and notes the central absentee voter precinct route alongside the city's instruction to go to the ward polling place. Also added the missing § 24.2-703.2 replacement ballot for voters with a disability or illness, with its Saturday close-of-business request deadline.

s12: 'a death in the family' was broader than § 24.2-705(A), which names the voter's hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness or death of a spouse, child or parent, or another emergency; and clause (ii) needs an emergency that arose after the application deadline. The § 24.2-705(B) route now gives its conditions: an obligation arising after 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before that requires absence from the city for business, profession or occupation, or for a hospitalization or death in the immediate family, or the officer-of-election case. It also gives the ID requirement of § 24.2-643 and points to the form's Sections 1a and 1b. Legal_basis entries were added for the representative's eligibility, the 5:00 p.m. form return and the close-of-polls receipt rule.

s5: 'Applications are accepted from 12 months before' is now 'may be accepted', with the later-date rule of § 24.2-701(A). Added that the last four Social Security digits are not required for an application completed in person (§ 24.2-701(C)(1)). The Department's identity-details list is now described as its guide for joining the permanent list online, which is what the page gives.

s3, s4, s1: s3 now gives the statutory weekend minimums of § 24.2-701.1(B) and the city's statement that it opens 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on the Saturday before every general election. s4's 'Accessible equipment is available on request' is not on the city pages read; it is now attributed to the Department's page, which says 'Accessible equipment and/or curbside voting is available upon request.' s1 adds the 10-day close of books (§ 24.2-416(A)) behind the October 23 deadline.

Forms: f4 (SBE-703.1C) had fillable null. Its AcroForm has an empty Fields array, so it is now recorded as not fillable, and the forms caveat is updated. The form numbers and revisions of f1, f3, f4 and f5 were confirmed from the PDFs (SBE-701/703.1 Rev. 7/2022, Spanish edition Rev. 7/2022, SBE-703.1C Rev. 4/2025, ELECT-705 Rev. 07/2026); f1, f3 and f5 have no form fields. The f5 title now describes both of the form's routes.

Escalation: rung 2 is limited to ballots received by the Friday before the election. Rung 4 uses the statute's family wording. In rung 5, the right to send ID or a signed statement is limited to voters who voted provisionally for lack of ID (§ 24.2-653(B)); any provisional voter may attend the meeting. Rung 6 adds that removal needs a material adverse effect on the conduct of the office (§ 24.2-109(B)) and is by petition to the circuit court (§ 24.2-234.1(B)), and that the city pages describe no complaint procedure. Rung 7 says § 24.2-706(G) does not name the venue.

Caveats: the access caveat now records that Internet Archive captures of other city pages from August to October 2026 are bot-challenge pages, and that the How to Vote menu lists a Vote By Mail page with no archived copy. New caveats cover the ELECT-705 postmark instruction against § 24.2-705(A), the replacement ballot form that was not located, the 1VAC20-70-20(F) postmark rule, the court venue inference, and the § 24.2-612 deadline against the Department's 'starting 45 days' wording. Sources were added for the six new Code sections and for the 2024 How to Vote capture that the forms caveat relies on.

Checked and confirmed without change: office location, directions, P.O. box, phone, email and regular hours (Voter Registration capture of July 17, 2026); the August 2026 primary schedule and the Saturday-before-general-elections hours; the 2025 start-date pattern (capture of November 14, 2025); the Where to Vote statements and 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. poll hours; the Electoral Board's general mailbox (members' individual mailboxes are on the page and are left out); the Upcoming Elections 'Stay tuned' note; the Department's November 3, 2026 dates (Upcoming Elections page), its contact page (phones, address, hours, the Election Day Complaint Form) and its Voter Identification chart Rev. 09/2026 (the ID list in s4); the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office phone, hours and address; the City Code § 1.10.010 paraphrase (eCode360 section page, which robots.txt allows; still not quoted); the 2024 city-hosted application link; the discovery fixture's October 23 note. No staff, board member or judge names, personal mailboxes or direct lines are recorded.
open_issues: The live city site was not read. www.ci.staunton.va.us answers HTTP 403 to the research User-Agent behind a bot check, and Internet Archive captures since August 2026 hold the challenge page. It was not read in a browser, since that would get past the bot check. So the city's notices for November 3, 2026 were not seen: hours for Sunday October 18, Saturday October 24 and Sunday October 25, the drop-off sites, and any satellite office. The steps give the state dates and statutory minimums and say the local details were not read, so no step is wrong as written; a person should confirm them on the live page or by phone.

The city's Vote By Mail page (www.ci.staunton.va.us/departments/voter-registration/how-to-vote/vote-by-mail) has no archived copy and was not read. It may list drop box, fax or email details that s5 and s9 leave open.
The State Board form for a § 24.2-703.2 replacement ballot was not located on the Department pages read; s11 tells voters to ask the office.

ELECT-705's instructions say the voted emergency ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, while § 24.2-705(A) counts it only if the registrar receives it before the polls close. The record follows the statute.

Sections 24.2-653, 24.2-706, 24.2-709, 24.2-709.1 and 24.2-711.1 end on January 1, 2027, and § 24.2-703.1 on July 1, 2027; the index holds no later text. This does not affect the November 3, 2026 election, but the file needs re-checking before later elections.
The Department's September 18 start is one day earlier than the 45th day under § 24.2-701.1(A) (September 19); the reason was not found. The city's 2025 schedule followed the same pattern.
